lift.desc: A loaded rucksack at the outer edge of what carries comfortably. 50 kg overhead is possible in short bursts; sustained hold causes tremor. Below the threshold that separates trained humans from the untrained.

strike.desc: 30 kgf. A firm shove made deliberate — leaves soft material depressions, bruises at contact. Below the threshold that breaks structural materials.

impact.desc: 0.1 m radius. A hard landing leaves a boot-shaped dent in soft soil. Concrete is unmarked. The environment does not register the arrival.

precision.desc: 0.03 — essentially no calibration. Force output is all-or-nothing. Holding a ceramic cup risks crushing it. Even simple grips require conscious bracing to avoid damage.

lift.desc: Peak human lifting ceiling — a bar loaded to 120 kg hoisted for a single clean press. Strong, but entirely mortal. Prolonged holds drain the body the way any maximum effort does.

strike.desc: 80 kgf. A well-thrown human punch at maximum extension. Soft pine splits; drywall dents but doesn't breach. The ceiling of what biology produces unaided.

impact.desc: 0.3 m radius. Packed earth compresses slightly underfoot. A heavy landing on tile will crack the tile. No collateral radius to speak of.

precision.desc: 0.05 — at peak human baseline, control is biological habit, not precision. Skilled craftwork is possible. Fragile materials are survivable. Under stress, output spikes unpredictably.

lift.desc: 800 kg: the mass of a small compact car lifted clear of the ground. Tires leave the pavement. It's not elegant, but the weight is controlled. Shaking under load is gone.

strike.desc: 500 kgf — the concentrated force of a small car collision at low urban speed. Standard concrete blocks develop hairline fractures at the impact point.

impact.desc: 0.5 m — a half-meter of cracked pavement radiates from a full-force stomp. Loose glass in nearby frames rattles. Surface concrete hairlines at the contact point.

precision.desc: 0.10 — the start of actual calibration. Glass objects can be picked up without risk if movement is slow and deliberate. Under pressure, the lower end of this control vanishes.

lift.desc: A metric tonne and change — a standard shipping pallet stacked full of dense cargo. The difference between this and a peak human is architectural. There's no comparison left.

strike.desc: 700 kgf. Unreinforced clay brick splits cleanly. Cast iron cookware shatters. The blow no longer needs momentum — static press force alone achieves structural failure in common materials.

impact.desc: 0.6 m radius. Cracked concrete no longer requires a deliberate stomp — any uncontrolled hard landing produces it. Nearby objects on the ground tip over.

precision.desc: 0.13 — fine motor calibration improves, but the gap between intent and output is still wide. Gripping a sparrow without harming it requires genuine concentration.

lift.desc: 1,400 kg in static overhead hold. Two stacked mid-size sedans. The wrists don't strain, the spine doesn't compress. The difficulty is a choice, not a limitation.

strike.desc: 950 kgf. At this threshold, standard wall materials — hollow-core masonry, timber frame panels — fail on first contact. Entry barriers stop being obstacles.

impact.desc: 0.8 m radius. Ground deformation visible as a raised ring of compressed material around the impact point. Unreinforced tile floors fracture in the zone.

precision.desc: 0.18 — the body is beginning to learn to throttle itself. In calm conditions, a lit candle can be moved without the flame bending. Under combat stress, that precision is the first thing to go.

lift.desc: 2,000 kg — the mass of a loaded passenger van, held overhead indefinitely. From here, 'heavy' stops being a meaningful word for anything at human scale.

strike.desc: 1,200 kgf: the force of a direct high-speed collision between passenger vehicles. Structural steel begins to deform. Reinforced doors and hatches buckle inward.

impact.desc: 1.0 m shockwave radius. A deliberate stomp cracks concrete slabs across a full meter. Vehicle windows in the immediate area vibrate audibly.

precision.desc: 0.30 — 30% calibration. Reliable enough for deliberate fine work, not for simultaneous action. Can hold the lower end while exerting elsewhere, but not both at the same time.

lift.desc: A small delivery truck, fully loaded: 2,200 kg. At this point the constraint is no longer the body — it's what's being lifted and whether it structurally survives the grip.

strike.desc: 1,500 kgf. A deliberate blow exceeds the yield point of most standard-grade steel sheet. Vault doors of the kind used in commercial buildings fail on a straight strike.

impact.desc: 1.0 m radius at E-rank entry — structurally similar to a heavy industrial drop test. Soil compresses 2–3 cm; loose surface objects displace.

precision.desc: 0.40 — the split between care and force is no longer an either/or choice. A handshake with a baseline human can be controlled reliably. Still a conscious act.

lift.desc: 3,200 kg — a medium-duty military transport emptied of its cargo. Ground vehicles stop being objects that are moved and start being objects that are thrown.

strike.desc: 2,200 kgf. The force equivalent of a bridge beam dropped from three meters — except focused to a contact point. Reinforced concrete posts crack through, not just chip.

impact.desc: 1.4 m radius. 4 cm of soil compression on landing. The surface ring of visible ground disruption is consistently wider than the foot area.

precision.desc: 0.45 — fine calibration at this level means a deliberate grip no longer risks damage to what it holds. High-output simultaneous is not yet possible — one at a time.

lift.desc: 4,200 kg in static hold. An armored personnel carrier. The mass is there, the resistance is not.

strike.desc: 3,000 kgf. A single blow at E+++ range deforms heavy structural I-beams. The mass of material struck matters less than its cross-sectional yield.

impact.desc: 1.7 m radius. Pavement cracks propagate outward from the contact zone. Light structures on the fringe of the radius register as vibration events.

precision.desc: 0.48 — sitting near the E-ceiling, the body has internalized low-output behavior enough that most civilian interactions don't require attention. Concentration reserved for high end.

lift.desc: 5,000 kg — a full-sized military IFV without its crew. At this upper E-rank ceiling, the body doesn't register the effort. The object strains before the person does.

strike.desc: 3,500 kgf — the equivalent of a wrecking ball's delivered impact. Reinforced masonry columns fracture at the contact zone; structural failure propagates outward.

impact.desc: 2.0 m shockwave radius. Soil deforms 5 cm on a standard landing. Standing water in the zone displaces outward. Nearby window panes crack under a full-force impact.

precision.desc: 0.50 — halfway on the calibration scale. The lower bound is effectively automatic. Moving through occupied spaces without damage is a background function, not a task.

lift.desc: 10,000 kg. A battle tank's turret assembly lifted clean. Industrial cranes move loads at this scale; here it's raw static force from two hands.

strike.desc: 8,000 kgf. Vehicle chassis crumple on contact; reinforced concrete columns split rather than crack. Heavy industrial machinery is no longer structurally relevant as resistance.

impact.desc: 3.0 m radius on full-force impact. A 20–30 cm crater forms in packed earth. Walls within the zone develop structural hairlines; unreinforced brick loses mortar cohesion.

precision.desc: 0.60 — upper-end calibration begins to emerge. Energy signature partially suppressible. Fine-motor work and full-force strike readiness are no longer mutually exclusive, though simultaneous is still costly.

lift.desc: 16,000 kg. A loaded main battle tank. At this scale, individual vehicles are not obstacles — they're objects. The limiting factor is grip surface, not output.

strike.desc: 14,000 kgf. The force equivalent of a loaded freight container dropped from height — but point-targeted. Bridge support struts deform. Blast doors breach.

impact.desc: 4.0 m radius. Craters in packed earth reach 35 cm depth. Vehicles within the zone roll or tip. Unreinforced masonry walls register the event as structural stress.

precision.desc: 0.64 — at this tier, the character can modulate continuously across the output range without visible transition gaps. Calibration has become habit rather than effort.

lift.desc: 24,000 kg: a fully armed attack helicopter, fuel and payload included. Scale of reference has shifted from vehicles to aircraft.

strike.desc: 19,000 kgf. Armored military vehicle hulls indent on a direct strike. The kind of force that mine detonations produce, applied through a fist.

impact.desc: 5.0 m radius. 45 cm of excavation depth on a deliberate full-force ground strike. Structural walls within the radius crack visibly; glass shatters across the zone.

precision.desc: 0.67 — the body no longer leaks force during idle movement. In a crowd, the environmental footprint is controlled automatically. Upper-end output requires intent, not permission.

lift.desc: 30,000 kg — a heavy combat helicopter or a stacked railroad freight section. At D-rank ceiling, the question is no longer whether it lifts. It's what breaks first, the object or the ground under the lifter.

strike.desc: 22,000 kgf. Equivalent to a direct hit from a large-caliber ship gun round in kinetic terms. Reinforced bunker entrances fail. Armored steel plate at NATO standard peels and folds.

impact.desc: 6.0 m radius at D ceiling. Full-force impact creates a 0.5 m crater in compacted ground. Unreinforced walls within the zone crack through, not just surface — they lose load-bearing capacity.

precision.desc: 0.70 — at D ceiling, fine control and suppression are both reliable without conscious allocation. The challenge is no longer 'can it be controlled' but 'what is the cost of maximum simultaneous range.'

lift.desc: 80,000 kg: a loaded freight locomotive. Overhead in static hold. The mass of an entire rail car, wheels to roof.

strike.desc: 60,000 kgf. At C-rank entry, individual artillery impacts are the appropriate comparison. Reinforced concrete shear walls fail on contact; structural cores crack.

impact.desc: 10 m radius. Unreinforced masonry fails structurally within the entire zone — not just cracks, collapses. Ground subsides 5–10 cm across the full radius on a standing full-force impact.

precision.desc: 0.80 — passive shield suppression mastered. The character operates at two ends of the output spectrum simultaneously, but only with deliberate focus. The cost is awareness, not effort.

lift.desc: 100,000 kg. The structural steel frame of a medium-sized building floor, stripped of concrete. Infrastructure rather than vehicles is the relevant scale.

strike.desc: 80,000 kgf. Tank armor is not resistant at this output. Hardened vehicle steel shatters at the point of contact rather than deforming.

impact.desc: 13 m radius. Reinforced concrete slabs within the zone fracture across their reinforcing bars. Vehicle traffic within range is thrown laterally by the pressure wave.

precision.desc: 0.83 — civilian-safe interaction in active environments requires no conscious overhead. Upper-end concentration of force is available immediately on demand.

lift.desc: 120,000 kg. A large naval patrol vessel displaced from water. The gap between this and peak D-rank is wider than the gap between peak human and lower D.

strike.desc: 95,000 kgf. The impact force of a naval shell delivered by a fist. Reinforced bridge decking fails. Military bunker structures develop structural cracks from a single blow.

impact.desc: 16 m radius. A shockwave at this scale propagates through surrounding building foundations, causing structural micro-damage beyond the visible radius.

precision.desc: 0.86 — the gap between full suppression and full output has collapsed to a single triggered decision. No ramp-up, no transition phase.

lift.desc: 150,000 kg — the displacement mass of a small warship, removed from its element entirely. Geological terminology hasn't entered yet. It's still engineering scale. Barely.

strike.desc: 110,000 kgf — at C-rank ceiling, a single blow carries more kinetic force than heavy artillery. The receiving material's composition becomes irrelevant; only mass and cross-section matter.

impact.desc: 20 m radius at C ceiling. The zone of structural failure extends to full masonry collapse across 20 meters. Ground displacement is visible from aerial vantage.

precision.desc: 0.88 — C ceiling. Full simultaneous control of lower and upper output bounds with deliberate focus. Not automatic — but the cost of focus is minimal and sustainable indefinitely.

lift.desc: 300,000 kg: a moderate ocean freighter's loaded displacement mass. At B-rank entry, the frame of reference has moved from construction to maritime shipping.

strike.desc: 220,000 kgf at B-rank entry. A blow that exceeds the penetration force of modern anti-tank weapons. Reinforced bunker walls breach with a single strike.

impact.desc: 50 m radius. Minor rockslides initiate on exposed slopes within the zone. Standard building frames buckle structurally at the zone edge rather than just cracking.

precision.desc: 0.92 — micro-gram touch threshold and peak-output strike readiness available as concurrent states. Scaling between them during a single physical motion is possible without loss.

lift.desc: 350,000 kg. Three fully loaded Boeing 747s stacked by mass. Aviation rather than maritime is the clearer comparison. The weight no longer communicates strain.

strike.desc: 290,000 kgf. The force delivered to a target matches or exceeds a large shaped charge detonation. Steel-reinforced bomb shelter walls fail structurally.

impact.desc: 80 m radius. A direct hit on urban ground collapses every standard construction building in the zone. Exposed rock faces fracture and shed debris.

precision.desc: 0.94 — at this precision level, force concentration can occur along individual fingers while the rest of the hand remains passive. Selective limb isolation begins.

lift.desc: 400,000 kg. The structural mass of a mid-size skyscraper's steel frame alone, excluding cladding and floors. Architecture replaces transportation as the unit of reference.

strike.desc: 340,000 kgf. Comparable to direct impact from a large naval round — the kind that pierces capital ship armor. From here, structural architecture is not a relevant defense.

impact.desc: 110 m radius. Earth excavates to over a meter depth at the epicenter; structural steel frames within the zone are no longer vertical at the boundary.

precision.desc: 0.96 — during high-velocity maneuver, output calibration degrades by less than one percent. Precision is not a slow-movement capability — it holds at speed.

lift.desc: 500,000 kg. Half a million kilograms — the mass of a completed 20-story residential block stripped to raw concrete and steel. At B-rank ceiling, buildings become liftable objects.

strike.desc: 380,000 kgf — B-rank ceiling. Bunker-penetrating ordnance on kinetic force comparison. Reinforced mountain tunnels fail at their weakest cross-section on a direct strike.

impact.desc: 150 m radius — B ceiling. The shockwave radius now swallows entire city blocks. Ground deformation is terrain-altering, not just structural.

precision.desc: 0.97 — B ceiling. Micro-gram to peak-output scaling in a single continuous motion, without interruption. No mechanical lag between the two ends of the range.

lift.desc: 1,000,000 kg. One million kilograms in overhead static hold — the mass of a medium commercial highrise from foundation cap to rooftop antenna. Geological scale is the next unit of measure.

strike.desc: 750,000 kgf at A-rank entry. A single deliberate blow carries force sufficient to shear a reinforced concrete dam structure at its weakest cross-section.

impact.desc: 300 m radius. Geological strata displace at the epicenter. Surface rock layers fracture to depth. Reinforced structures at the zone edge lose structural integrity.

precision.desc: 0.98 — zero parasitic energy loss at any output level. Force applied exactly where directed, nothing bleeds into adjacent surfaces. Adjacent materials survive full-output strikes against the one between them.

lift.desc: 2,000,000 kg. The mass of a reinforced dam section — a load that requires tunneling equipment to move by conventional means. From here, the vocabulary shifts to geological.

strike.desc: 1,600,000 kgf. The force equivalent of a large-tonnage ship anchor dropped from cruise altitude — concentrated to contact. Geological strata at the surface crack and displace.

impact.desc: 500 m radius. The impact zone reshapes local terrain — not just ground deformation, but topographical change. Sub-surface rock layers crack and shift.

precision.desc: 0.985 — at A-rank mid, different limbs operate at different output levels simultaneously without channel interference. A caress and a demolition strike can occur in the same second.

lift.desc: 3,500,000 kg. A section of mountain road cut from the cliff face, entire, including substrate — the kind of mass that requires months of blasting to separate from bedrock.

strike.desc: 2,500,000 kgf. Sub-surface rock layers fracture and shift at the strike zone. The environmental consequence of a direct hit at full output is geological, not structural.

impact.desc: 650 m radius. Geological fracture lines propagate from the epicenter. Rock overhangs and cliff faces within range shear and collapse under the transmitted shockwave.

precision.desc: 0.99 — surgical and macro-scale outputs operate as fully independent systems. One hand can be threading a needle while the other splits bedrock, without the two interfering.

lift.desc: 5,000,000 kg. A small hill's surface strata or a dense urban city block stripped to its foundations. Mass that civil engineering plans around, not over.

strike.desc: 3,500,000 kgf — A-rank ceiling. A single blow displaces surface strata and compresses bedrock below the contact depth. The strike event registers seismically at distance.

impact.desc: 800 m radius — A ceiling. Localized geological strata displacement across the full zone. The impact event reads as a seismic signature at regional monitoring stations.

precision.desc: 0.99 — A ceiling. Zero parasitic energy loss across all kinetic applications. Output is expressed precisely as intended, no more, no less, regardless of the scale or speed of the action.

lift.desc: 7,000,000 kg — the dense core of a mid-sized geological formation. Mechanical extraction of this mass takes industrial-grade equipment weeks. Static hold is effortless.

strike.desc: 5,500,000 kgf. At S-rank entry, individual strikes begin generating ground-level seismic signatures. Surface rock layers shear and displace around the contact zone.

impact.desc: 1.2 km radius. Seismic activity up to 3.5 Richter generated at impact. The terrain within the zone is not the same terrain after — surface topology changes permanently.

precision.desc: 1.00 — S entry. Precision has passed the 'factor' scale. Full simultaneous macro-demolition and surgical-scale allocation operate as independent channels with no shared overhead.

lift.desc: 10,000,000 kg. A large rocky promontory. At S-rank entry, the vocabulary of lift shifts from architecture and transport to geology. Outcroppings and cliff faces are the reference point.

strike.desc: 7,500,000 kgf. The force equivalent of a large coastal landslide compressed to point impact. Fault lines near the strike zone respond.

impact.desc: 1.0 km radius at S entry. Seismic reading up to 4.0 Richter. Slope collapse, surface rock shearing, and subsurface fracture propagation all occur simultaneously within the zone.

precision.desc: 1.00 — at this tier, precision is not a capability that's exercised — it's the default state. Output at any scale on any limb does not affect adjacent outputs.

lift.desc: 20,000,000 kg. The mass of a small island's topsoil and surface rock layer across several hectares.

strike.desc: 15,000,000 kgf. Cliff face geology fractures from impact vibration, not just the contact zone. Strike events trigger slope collapse on exposed terrain nearby.

impact.desc: 2.0 km radius. Terrain-scale disruption — rivers redirect, cliff faces collapse, valley walls fracture. Ground within the zone subsides or uplifts unevenly.

precision.desc: 1.00 — city-scale destruction and sub-millimeter force application can occur in the same breath. Collateral output, by this point, is always intentional.

lift.desc: 30,000,000 kg. A dense surface rock formation spanning tens of meters in all dimensions. Mountains are the approaching unit of measure.

strike.desc: 23,000,000 kgf. The kind of point force that reshapes river gorge walls. Solid granite shatters, not cracks. Secondary debris fields form from the shockwave alone.

impact.desc: 3.0 km radius. The kind of geological disruption that requires years of satellite monitoring to fully document. Seismic 4.2 Richter class.

precision.desc: 1.00 — zero channel interference across all bodily extremities. Precision is not something applied; it is the operational baseline from which deviation requires deliberate choice.

lift.desc: 40,000,000 kg. A large, isolated geological peak stripped from its base — if such a thing were physically separable. The effort is not the lift; it's the grip.

strike.desc: 32,000,000 kgf. Subsurface rock layers fracture meters below the strike point. A full-force blow reshapes local terrain in a way that survives for decades.

impact.desc: 4.0 km radius. Regional geography is altered by a full-force impact. The event is registered by tectonic monitoring networks.

precision.desc: 1.00 — at mid-S, the concept of 'control' has inverted: maximum destructive output is constrained, not released. Destruction is a precision act, not a failure of it.

lift.desc: 45,000,000 kg. Mid-mountain mass. A mountain ridge's protruding rock cap rather than its full body. From here to SS is an order of magnitude climb.

strike.desc: 37,000,000 kgf. Tectonic surface features respond — not initiated, but stressed into micro-movement. The planet registers the event at shallow seismic monitoring depth.

impact.desc: 4.5 km radius. Seismic 4.3 Richter at impact. The zone of effect is large enough that the far edge experiences a different geological outcome than the epicenter.

precision.desc: 1.00 — simultaneous micro-vibrational and macro-kinetic outputs run on independent tracks. The system does not differentiate between them in terms of cognitive load.

lift.desc: 50,000,000 kg at S-rank ceiling. The full visible mass of a substantial rock peak — not the mountain, but the topmost geological body. Continental scale is one rank away.

strike.desc: 40,000,000 kgf — S-rank ceiling. A single unrestrained strike causes 4.5 Richter class seismic activity at the impact zone. Terrain is permanently altered.

impact.desc: 5.0 km radius at S ceiling. Full-force impact generates 4.5 Richter seismic activity. Terrain reshaping is regional, not local.

precision.desc: 1.00 — S ceiling. Precision is not a field that scales further — it has been fully resolved. What changes at SS and SSS is scale, not calibration quality.

lift.desc: 200,000,000 kg. The jump from S-rank ceiling to this point is the first genuinely tectonic transition — the kind of mass that would register as a seismic anomaly if displaced.

strike.desc: 120,000,000 kgf. The mass of a compressed continental impact equivalent. Individual mountains begin to be the structural benchmark.

impact.desc: 7.5 km radius. Transition to SS-tier impact character — the zone begins generating island-scale surface disruption. Seismic reading 5.0 Richter.

precision.desc: 1.00 — full simultaneous output control across extremities, sustained indefinitely. Micro-adjustment and continental-scale output coexist without interference.

lift.desc: 500,000,000 kg. Island-scale geological mass begins here. Not a peak, not a ridge — the kind of volume that cartographers label separately from the surrounding terrain.

strike.desc: 400,000,000 kgf at SS-rank entry. The force of a major tectonic stress event — not triggered by plates, but by a deliberate blow. Geography reshapes around the contact.

impact.desc: 10 km radius at SS entry. Permanent geological alteration across the full zone. Seismic activity up to 5.5 Richter. Coastal shorelines within range shift.

precision.desc: 1.00 — SS entry. The precision of a jeweler applied to the forces of a geological event. Both are available in the same moment, deployed independently.

lift.desc: 900,000,000 kg. The mass of a small inhabited island's primary land body, excluding its subsurface shelf.

strike.desc: 700,000,000 kgf. Coastal geography bends. Island shorelines shift from a direct impact strike at maximum output.

impact.desc: 15 km radius. Island-scale surface alteration — the zone of effect is large enough to encompass a small inhabited island entirely.

precision.desc: 1.00 — at this range, individual cells within a grip can be pressed at different pressures simultaneously. The concept of 'output leak' has been structurally eliminated.

lift.desc: 1,500,000,000 kg. Multiple islands compacted to mass — or a continental peninsula's protruding surface geology. Geography is the reference frame now, not geology.

strike.desc: 1,100,000,000 kgf. A single blow carries the concentrated force of a mid-tier tectonic convergence event. Continental margin fractures record the event.

impact.desc: 25 km radius. Seismic 6.0 Richter. Continental shelf edges within the zone fracture and shift. Impact displaces enough material to alter the local sea floor.

precision.desc: 1.00 — force output is expressed with the same resolution across all scales. What is intended is what occurs. Nothing more, nothing less, regardless of magnitude.

lift.desc: 2,000,000,000 kg. The kind of mass that, if displaced, would alter regional coastal maps. Island chains rather than individual peaks.

strike.desc: 1,500,000,000 kgf. Mountain ranges fracture at their geological fault lines from the shockwave, not just the contact point.

impact.desc: 35 km radius. Mountain ranges within the zone register primary fractures along their geological fault lines. Atmospheric pressure wave visible from adjacent terrain.

precision.desc: 1.00 — force calibration at SS mid is a non-issue. Precision consumes no overhead. The challenge is no longer control but the management of World Rejection accumulation from high-output events.

lift.desc: 2,500,000,000 kg. A small atoll archipelago in total surface mass. The lifter no longer operates at the scale of geological events — they are one.

strike.desc: 1,750,000,000 kgf. Island-scale permanent geological alteration from one blow. Seismic monitoring at 6.0 Richter at impact.

impact.desc: 42 km radius. A sustained full-force impact at this level reshapes country-scale geography. Seismic 6.3 Richter across the zone.

precision.desc: 1.00 — micro-vibrational adjustment and island-scale kinetic force deployed across independent bodily extremities simultaneously. No mechanical lag at any output tier.

lift.desc: 2,750,000,000 kg. Approaching the total mass of a densely populated island city-state, land surface only. Not lifted from ground — lifted from the ocean floor up.

strike.desc: 1,900,000,000 kgf. Impact events at this force level alter regional geography in ways that render existing maps inaccurate.

impact.desc: 47 km radius. Island chains within the zone are geologically altered as a single event. Atmospheric shockwave audible at intercontinental distances.

precision.desc: 1.00 — at this level, 'precision' is better described as perfect expression. There is no measurable gap between intended and actual output at any scale.

lift.desc: 3,000,000,000 kg. Three billion kilograms at SS-rank ceiling — the surface mass of a small inhabited island in full. A geopolitical entity measured in weight.

strike.desc: 2,000,000,000 kgf at SS ceiling. A single maximum strike triggers 6.5 Richter class seismic activity. The strike site is no longer geologically continuous with its surroundings.

impact.desc: 50 km radius at SS ceiling. Seismic 6.5 Richter. Permanent geological alteration within island-scale zones. Atmospheric displacement is measurable from orbit.

precision.desc: 1.00 — SS ceiling. Simultaneous micro-quantum adjustment and maximum tectonic load deployment. The only operational constraint is not precision — it is World Rejection tolerance.

lift.desc: 26,500,000,000 kg. Transition between SS and SSS ceiling: the mass of a major island nation's entire above-sea-level landmass.

strike.desc: 13,000,000,000 kgf. The threshold between SS and SSS ceiling: force that compresses bedrock layers and propagates continental-scale surface fractures.

impact.desc: 65 km radius. Transition to SSS ceiling — tectonic surface features within the zone begin separating from their base strata.

precision.desc: 1.00 — transitioning to SSS. Precision is structural, not behavioral — it does not vary with conditions, fatigue, or distraction.

lift.desc: 50,000,000,000 kg. At SSS-rank entry, the reference is not islands but continental shelves — subsurface rock slabs the size of small nations.

strike.desc: 40,000,000,000 kgf at SSS entry. The force equivalent of a deep crustal rupture concentrated to a fist-sized contact area. Atmospheric displacement is measurable from altitude.

impact.desc: 50 km radius at SSS entry (concentrated force — shockwave tightens as output density increases). Continental-scale structural fracturing propagates from the epicenter. Atmospheric displacement from low orbit.

precision.desc: 1.00 — at SSS entry, the body expresses force at atomic resolution if required. Deliberate and incidental outputs are distinguished at the level of individual molecular bonds.

lift.desc: 100,000,000,000 kg. The mass of a large mountain range's primary ridgeline geology. Individual peaks become sub-units of the relevant scale.

strike.desc: 80,000,000,000 kgf. Individual tectonic plates flex at their boundaries from the transmitted force. The strike registers from low orbit instrumentation.

impact.desc: 120 km radius. Continental plate surfaces fracture and partially separate within the zone. Seismic signatures register globally.

precision.desc: 1.00 — precision at SSS mid extends to energy itself: output can be directed not just in force but in dimensional orientation, expressed within or against the fabric of local space.

lift.desc: 150,000,000,000 kg. The rock mass of a significant portion of a continental interior plateau. Geological epochs are the relevant framing for what's being shifted.

strike.desc: 120,000,000,000 kgf. Continental crust bends — not breaks, bends — at the strike site under full-force impact. The planet's surface geometry changes locally.

impact.desc: 180 km radius. The shockwave propagation at this scale interacts with existing fault systems, triggering secondary events beyond the primary zone.

precision.desc: 1.00 — all bodily extremities operate as fully independent precision instruments. Zero channel interference. Zero mechanical lag. Output architecture is perfectly expressive at every scale.

lift.desc: 190,000,000,000 kg. An entire mountain chain, surface-to-bedrock separation, theoretical but within output range.

strike.desc: 160,000,000,000 kgf. Strikes at this force level reshape continental surface geology in a single event. Equivalent to a major subduction stress release, point-applied.

impact.desc: 220 km radius. Full-force impact at this tier alters the surface topography of a continental interior. The event is non-reversible by any natural process on a human timescale.

precision.desc: 1.00 — the full precision range — from contact force measured in milligrams to tectonic-class output — is simultaneously available without transition. The selection is instantaneous.

lift.desc: 220,000,000,000 kg. The mass of a continental interior rift valley's rock column, full depth. Tectonic plates are the approaching frame of reference.

strike.desc: 190,000,000,000 kgf. The force required to shear surface strata from a continent's interior plateau in a single strike. Seismically equivalent to a magnitude 8+ event.

impact.desc: 260 km radius. Tectonic plates bend rather than break at the zone edge — the force is distributed too widely for simple fracture. The center is a different story.

precision.desc: 1.00 — force at any scale is geometrically exact. Adjacent materials, adjacent dimensions, and adjacent biological systems are unaffected by anything that wasn't directed at them.

lift.desc: 250,000,000,000 kg — a quarter of a trillion kilograms. The surface mass of a large sub-continental landmass. Not a feature of the planet. A fragment of it.

strike.desc: 200,000,000,000 kgf at SSS mid-range. A deliberate blow delivers a force that, spread across a fault system, would trigger a continental-scale tectonic event. Here it's one contact point.

impact.desc: 300 km radius at SSS mid. The atmospheric displacement column from this impact is visible as a permanent feature from low orbit for days afterward.

precision.desc: 1.00 — SSS mid-range. Precision operates at a level where the distinction between 'focused' and 'suppressed' has dissolved — it's all the same resolution, at any output.

lift.desc: 340,000,000,000 kg. Beyond any natural surface feature isolatable as a single object. The relevant unit is now 'portion of tectonic plate.'

strike.desc: 270,000,000,000 kgf. At this scale, the atmosphere around the impact zone displaces visibly before contact completes. Shockwave energy exceeds the structural threshold of any surface material.

impact.desc: 310 km radius. Tectonic surface layers fold at the zone boundary. Deep crustal rock comes to surface in the immediate vicinity of impact.

precision.desc: 1.00 — beyond this tier, precision continues at full resolution regardless of scale or World Rejection pressure. Maximum tectonic output and sub-atomic adjustment coexist in the same moment.

lift.desc: 430,000,000,000 kg. Continental crust sections. The act of lifting at this scale would register as a regional seismic anomaly from observation thousands of kilometers away.

strike.desc: 350,000,000,000 kgf. The force of a planetary-scale geological stress event applied through a single directed strike. No natural material absorbs this — it transmits, fractures, and disperses.

burst.desc: Range: 291 m. Reinforced structural frames within blast radius fail on a direct hit. AoE expression has acquired selective targeting — the energy can be released in chosen directions simultaneously.

aura.desc: Detectable at 166 m. AoE energy release capability is active — the aura occasionally releases omni-directionally rather than maintaining clean directional expression. Suppression is a continuous active task at C mid.

burst.desc: Range: 375 m. At C mid, technique discharge is capable of building-complex-scale structural failure in a single activation. Battlefield Command Aura operates from the same output layer.

duration.desc: Peak: 13 hours; moderate: 3.7 days. Recovery: 75 minutes. Area-of-Effect energy release is now active — energy discharges without requiring a direction. The technique library has expanded, and expanded techniques mean more chain capacity. Chain: 37.

aura.desc: Detectable at 183 m. The aura is complex enough at this tier that arc-scale instruments can partially read Core type from its signature. Suppression is standard operating procedure.

burst.desc: Range: 450 m. Mental resistance to external influence is active — the same outward energy expression that defines burst has an inward equivalent. Technique discharge at this range reshapes local terrain.

aura.desc: Detectable at 200 m. C ceiling — visible luminescence detectable without instruments at close range. Passive shield generates continuous environmental emission. Suppression required to prevent ambient structural damage.

burst.desc: Range: 500 m. C ceiling — AoE release fully capable, unreinforced masonry collapses within blast radius, directed discharge at 500 m. The Furnace provides this continuously without reserve degradation.

Visible to unaugmented baseline humans without focus. Continuous passive emission disturbs weather within 100 m. Suppression required.

burst.desc: Range: 1 km. Minor rockslides and building structural collapse triggered within blast radius. City-scale energy output achievable at maximum activation. The Star's floating reserve provides depth behind each technique discharge.

burst.desc: Range: 1.5 km. Sustained flight powered by Core operates independently of burst channel. Passive Essence absorption partially replenishes burst reserves between activations. Structural collapse zone extends with range.

aura.desc: Detectable at 450 m. City-scale energy output achievable — the aura at this sub-tier carries the potential energy density that reflects this. Weather disturbance within 100 m. Weak-willed individuals register physical pressure.

burst.desc: Range: 2 km. The Cell Lattice provides whole-body discharge surface — technique energy isn't funneled through a single output point but expressed across the entire body simultaneously. City-scale output at maximum activation.

aura.desc: Detectable at 525 m. The Cell Lattice — energy-conductive cytoskeleton in every cell — means emission is now a whole-body phenomenon, not a Core-surface one. Suppression must address every cell, not just the Core surface.

burst.desc: Range: 2.5 km. At B mid-upper, single-activation discharge creates a permanent alteration to the local terrain within the blast zone. Rockslides, foundation failure, surface rupture.

duration.desc: Peak: 7 days; moderate: 5 weeks. Recovery: 30 minutes. Chain: 100. B ceiling — city-scale energy output possible. Sustained flight powered by Core runs in parallel with full output without competing for reserves.

aura.desc: Detectable at 600 m. B ceiling — passive aura visible without focus. Weather patterns within 100 m disturbed continuously. Suppression required in civilian environments. Animals flee. Aura is now the person's visible constant.

burst.desc: Range: 3 km. B ceiling — city-scale energy output achievable at maximum activation. Minor rockslides and structural collapse within blast radius at full range. The discharge from B ceiling carries enough energy to change the face of an urban district in a single activation.

aura.desc: Detectable at 2.3 km. Domain-level energy expression means the aura is not a passive leak — it is a low-output domain boundary at rest. Atmospheric effects within 300 m measurable without instruments.

burst.desc: Range: 10 km. Geological strata displacement and surface terrain reshaping within blast radius on maximum discharge. Shockwave radius 600 m. Major AoE environmental control active from the same energy layer.

aura.desc: Detectable at 3 km. A ceiling — sustained full output without suppression begins drawing atmospheric response. Suppression near population centers is standard. The aura is a scaled-down expression of the same energy that powers geological-strata displacement.

burst.desc: Range: 15 km. A ceiling — geological strata displacement, shockwave radius 800 m. Consecutive maximum discharges deplete reserves measurably. The same energy that powers this burst powers domain-scale reality alteration.

duration.desc: Peak: 1 month; moderate: 1 year. The Twin provides dual output channels. Energy starvation without sufficient dungeon intake causes involuntary destructive ambient pull from surroundings — a hungry S-rank near civilians is dangerous without active suppression. Recovery for moderate techniques: under 5 minutes.

Unsuppressed full aura begins triggering World Rejection response. F-rank Corebearers cannot approach within 50 m without suppression active. Suppression required.

aura.desc: Detectable at 7.5 km. Core Bifurcation means the aura carries simultaneous city-scale and surgical-scale signatures — instruments read both channels as a complex overlay. Continuous active suppression required in inhabited areas.

burst.desc: Range: 47.5 km. Seismic 3.6 Richter. Shockwave radius 2 km. World Rejection accumulation per discharge is measurable — the system tracks exposure, not just output.

aura.desc: Detectable at 10 km. Regional deterrent-class energy output — the aura carries the potential density of this output as its resting signature. Unsuppressed full aura triggers measurable World Rejection response: atmospheric disturbance, localized spatial instability.

burst.desc: Range: 58.5 km. Seismic 4.0 Richter. Shockwave radius 3 km. Regional deterrent-class power output — a single maximum discharge at this range is a strategic event, not a tactical one.

aura.desc: Detectable at 12.5 km. Near-immortality while both Cores intact — the aura signature is recognized as a dual-Core continuous emission by those with instruments capable of the reading. World Rejection response escalates with aura strength.

burst.desc: Range: 67.5 km. Seismic 4.3 Richter. Shockwave 4 km. Near-immortality while both Cores intact — the entity deploying this burst is nearly impossible to remove as a threat by anything below S-tier.

duration.desc: Peak: 4 months; moderate: 2 years. Recovery for moderate: under 5 minutes. Full-scale: hours. S ceiling — heavy reality-warping within wide radius. The full-scale activation ceiling is not energy-limited so much as World Rejection-limited at peak.

aura.desc: Detectable at 15 km. S ceiling — permanent local weather effect in area of presence. Continuous active suppression required. Failure to suppress in populated areas draws escalating World Rejection regardless of intent.

burst.desc: Range: 80 km. Seismic 4.5 Richter. Shockwave 5 km. S ceiling — sequential full discharges draw increasing World Rejection response. Deploying multiple maximum discharges is a geopolitical-scale decision.

duration.desc: Peak: 3 days before World Rejection escalation; moderate: months. The Webwork distributes load efficiently but does not eliminate depletion. Internal exhaustion after 3 months continuous moderate output without replenishment. Full-scale: hours, not indefinitely.

Active suppression required at all times in inhabited regions. Unsuppressed aura triggers World Rejection cascade.

burst.desc: Range: 200 km. Seismic 5.5 Richter. Shockwave radius 10 km. Mountain-range-scale structural damage at upper range boundary. Consecutive full discharges at this scale accelerate World Rejection accumulation significantly. The Webwork means each discharge is a system-wide output event.

duration.desc: Peak: 10 days; moderate: months without replenishment. The Primordial Thread network allows simultaneous output across all bodily systems without channel competition — the depletion that occurs is on the aggregate reserve, not individual channels.

burst.desc: Range: 292.5 km. Seismic 5.8 Richter. Shockwave 20 km. The Primordial Thread network distributes technique energy across the full body for each discharge — the output surface is every cell in the body simultaneously.

aura.desc: Detectable at 106 km. At SS mid, the aura is visible as atmospheric distortion from kilometers away without instrumentation. The World's Rejection breakthrough was survived, but the world's ongoing objection to this tier's existence is expressed through the aura's environmental consequences.

burst.desc: Range: 356 km. Seismic 6.0 Richter. Shockwave 28 km. At SS mid, a single maximum discharge is a permanent geological event. Island-scale terrain alteration within blast radius.

duration.desc: Peak: 24 days; moderate: months. Near-absolute strategic perception and control are active. The technique chains at SS tier are limited not by activation count but by the depth each activation draws from the reserve.

aura.desc: Detectable at 125 km. Nation-level destructive potential, even passively — the aura carries that potential as its resting signature. Suppression failure in populated areas draws escalating World Rejection regardless of intent.

burst.desc: Range: 425 km. Seismic 6.3 Richter. Shockwave 37 km. Near-absolute strategic perception and control means discharge deployment is architecturally precise at these ranges — the outcome is known before the activation completes.

duration.desc: Peak: 30 days; moderate: indefinite with replenishment. Internal exhaustion after 6 months continuous moderate output without replenishment. SS ceiling — the World Rejection response to peak output determines the practical ceiling more than the internal reserve does.

aura.desc: Detectable at 150 km. SS ceiling — aura visible as atmospheric distortion from kilometers away. Any suppression lapse immediately triggers World Rejection cascade. Active suppression is permanent standard operating procedure.

burst.desc: Range: 500 km. Seismic 6.5 Richter. Shockwave 50 km. SS ceiling — regional seismic events triggered. Mountain-range-scale structural damage at upper range. Each full discharge accumulates World Rejection — strategic pacing is required.

duration.desc: Moderate output: indefinite through environmental conversion cycling. Full-scale: 6 hours before World Rejection approaches ejection threshold. Core reset required: 24 hours. Continental-scale activations are enormously expensive per use — two to three consecutive maximum discharges push near ejection threshold.

aura.desc: Detectable at 500 km. The Collapse — body inside the Core — means the aura is not emitted from the body but expressed by the Core anchor in Soul Space. Suppression required constantly. Any lapse triggers World Rejection cascade: spatial distortion, dimensional micro-tears, atmospheric tribulation within hundreds of km.

burst.desc: Range: 1,000 km. Tectonic events and continental-scale structural fracturing possible at maximum output. Shockwave radius 50 km. Each full discharge accumulates World Rejection — two to three consecutive maximum discharges push near ejection threshold. The Collapse means the discharge draws from the Core anchor, not from biological reserves.

duration.desc: Moderate: indefinite. Full-scale: 16 hours before ejection threshold. The Collapse placed the body inside the Core — the energy architecture that this creates is not a fixed reserve but a continuous conversion process. The ceiling is World Rejection tolerance, not stored energy.

aura.desc: Detectable at 875 km. The Unmaking rebuilt the body from atoms up — the aura of what was rebuilt carries the energetic signature of an entity that has died and returned. Full unsuppressed aura sustained for more than minutes accelerates ejection threshold accumulation.

burst.desc: Range: 1,750 km. Shockwave 112 km. Continental-scale structural fracturing. Atmospheric displacement visible from low orbit at upper range. The Unmaking established that this tier's output has a different relationship with physical limits — the discharge reflects that.

duration.desc: Moderate: indefinite. Full-scale: 26 hours. At SSS mid, the limitation on full-scale sustained output is the world treating the Corebearer as an existential foreign object. The internal energy supply is not the limiting factor.

aura.desc: Detectable at 1,250 km. At SSS mid, the aura is visible as atmospheric anomaly from hundreds of km without instrumentation. Continental-scale domain expression is active — the aura is the domain's resting surface expression.

burst.desc: Range: 2,000 km. Shockwave 175 km. At SSS mid, maximum discharge is a planetary-scale geological event. Consecutive activations are geopolitical decisions with world-tolerance stakes, not tactical ones.

duration.desc: Moderate: indefinite. Full-scale: 38 hours. Long-term reality engineering is active — not just altering but building. This class of activation is the most expensive per use and has the highest World Rejection cost per activation.

aura.desc: Detectable at 1,625 km. The aura at SSS upper carries the signature of an entity that is selecting what rules apply to it within its range. The World Rejection response to this is proportional — the world objects to that selection.

burst.desc: Range: 2,500 km. Shockwave 237 km. Long-term reality engineering active — maximum discharge is one element of a toolkit that also includes building, not just destroying. The cost per use remains at near-ejection-threshold for consecutive maximum deployments.

duration.desc: Moderate: indefinite. Full-scale: 48 hours before ejection threshold. SSS ceiling — capacity to choose what rules apply within continental domain. The most expensive activations at this tier aren't measured in energy at all — they're measured in world-tolerance budget per use.

aura.desc: Detectable at 2,000 km. SSS ceiling — active suppression required constantly within continental inhabited range. Any lapse immediately triggers World Rejection cascade. The aura is the footprint of a continental-scale domain at rest.

burst.desc: Range: 3,000 km. Shockwave 300 km. SSS ceiling — continental-scale fracturing on maximum output. Atmospheric displacement visible from low orbit. Two to three consecutive maximum discharges approach ejection threshold regardless of reserves.

jump.desc: 1.5 m vertical clearance, 3 m horizontal at sprint. The Seed's cardiovascular restructuring has marginally improved explosive leg output. A chain-link fence is clearable with a running start.
2 m vertical clearance, 5 m horizontal. The Venous Burn has distributed energy more evenly through the lower body. A second-story window ledge is reachable from ground level with focused effort.
2.5 m vertical clearance, 7 m horizontal. The wider venous network provides a more complete energy delivery to the leg muscles at the moment of explosive output. Single-story rooftop clearable.

3 m vertical clearance, 10 m horizontal. F ceiling — the Seed at this sub-tier provides enough explosive leg output to clear most standard building floors in a single jump. Still purely ballistic — no air control.

6 m vertical clearance, 15 m horizontal. The Pulse's sync with the heartbeat has turned the jump explosive threshold into a technique trigger — jump output aligns with the pulse burst for maximum efficiency.

10 m vertical clearance, 22 m horizontal. The bone channel network provides a structural spring storage mechanism — energy accumulates in the bone lattice during the crouch phase and releases at launch.

14 m vertical clearance, 30 m horizontal. Mid-air directional adjustment using Core output pressure — the first indication of flight as an eventual capability. Three-to-four-story buildings clearable in a single jump.
20 m vertical clearance, 40 m horizontal. E ceiling — the bone channel structure and energy shell forming around the Core provide a combined launch reservoir. Mid-air directional adjustment reliable.

40 m vertical clearance, 80 m horizontal. The Engine's constant hum provides a sustained launch energy — not a peak-then-drop but a continuous-force release through the jump arc. Controlled descent via Core output.
75 m vertical clearance, 150 m horizontal. The Ichor-Enriched Plasma's energy density provides leg-muscle peak output that dwarfs what biological tissue can sustain. Controlled descent standard.

115 m vertical clearance, 250 m horizontal. Complex elemental manipulation allows the jump arc to be reshaped mid-flight — not just direction correction but arc modification. Multi-story descent landing no longer impacts.
150 m vertical clearance, 350 m horizontal. At D mid-upper, the jump is functionally a controlled ballistic transit. Mid-air arc modification standard. Landing impact eliminated.

200 m vertical clearance, 450 m horizontal. D ceiling — jump output has exceeded the height of most skyscraper structures. Arc modification mid-flight, controlled descent, no landing impact. The foundation for C-rank flight is visible here.

flight.desc: 200 km/h horizontal, 500 m ceiling altitude. The Furnace generates enough continuous upward Core pressure to sustain powered flight. First tier with genuine flight — not ballistic transit but continuous controlled airborne movement. Maneuverability limited at high speed.

360 km/h, 1,200 m ceiling. The passive shield contributes lift stability — the energy layer that causes ambient environmental damage when unsuppressed also provides a platform for directional flight control. Aerobatic maneuvers possible.

550 km/h, 2,500 m ceiling. Intent is now a physical force — the same directional quality of will that drives outward technique expression drives flight path. Tight urban aerial navigation at this speed is achievable with full maneuverability.
700 km/h, 4,000 m ceiling. AoE energy release active — the flight engine and technique discharge channel are no longer separate budgets. Extended flight duration limited only by Core reserve.

900 km/h, 6,000 m ceiling. C ceiling flight — commercial jet cruise speed. The Furnace's continuous output is fully sufficient to maintain flight at this speed and altitude indefinitely at moderate energy expenditure.

1,850 km/h — Mach 1.5, 12,000 m ceiling. The Star's floating independent Core provides a dedicated flight energy source. Sonic boom left at full flight sprint. The body navigates supersonic air as a standard flight medium.
2,600 km/h — Mach 2.1, 18,000 m. Lungs supplementing breath with Essence absorption means flight doesn't compete with technique output — separate channels. Combat aircraft territory.

3,100 km/h — Mach 2.5, 25,000 m. Cell Lattice restructuring means the body's surface tolerates supersonic air friction as a normal environmental condition. The flight medium at this altitude is the stratosphere.
3,400 km/h — Mach 2.8, 30,000 m. Near-death recovery possible during sustained flight — the body maintains combat integrity while airborne at supersonic speed. Stratospheric flight standard.

3,700 km/h — Mach 3, 35,000 m. B ceiling — SR-71 Blackbird speed at stratospheric altitude. The Cell Lattice and Star combination provide the power density for indefinite flight at this ceiling. Sonic boom geometry visible from ground.

5,000 km/h — Mach 4, 50,000 m. The Fusion has threaded Core filaments through the torso — flight energy is drawn from the Core-torso integration rather than a single point source. Hypersonic flight. Plasma formation on leading edges at this speed and altitude range.

6,500 km/h — Mach 5.3, 65,000 m. Domain-level energy expression means the flight envelope is partially a localized reality — the conditions the body defines for itself include the aerodynamic parameters of movement. Scramjet speed range.

7,800 km/h — Mach 6.4, 75,000 m. At A mid, the body moves at hypersonic speeds at mesospheric altitude. Thermal scorch trails form behind flight path. The aerodynamic challenge is not drag — it is navigational precision at this velocity.
9,000 km/h — Mach 7.4, 85,000 m. Passive ambient Essence absorption begins during flight — the body partially self-replenishes during extended hypersonic transit. Re-entry vehicle territory.

9,880 km/h — Mach 8, 100,000 m. A ceiling — the Kármán line. Flight at orbital-boundary altitude at Mach 8. Atmospheric plasma envelope at this altitude and speed. The transition from flight to orbital transit is technically one step away.

11,115 km/h — Mach 9.1, 200 km altitude. The Twin — dual Core — provides a flight channel that is structurally independent from the combat output channel. Flight at low orbital altitude. The world curves visibly below.

13,000 km/h — Mach 10.6, 300 km altitude. Core Bifurcation means sustained flight at near-orbital speed runs without competing with technique output. Low Earth Orbit altitude range. Flight path traces planetary curvature.

14,500 km/h — Mach 11.8, 400 km altitude. Flight at the altitude of the International Space Station orbital range. No atmospheric medium — Core provides all propulsion and life support. Regional deterrent-class power deployed from this altitude.

16,000 km/h — Mach 13.1, 500 km altitude. Deep LEO range. Flight at this altitude requires Core-sustain for life support and propulsion simultaneously. The planetary surface is continuous terrain from here — all of it within direct observation.

17,290 km/h — Mach 14.1, 600 km altitude. S ceiling — low orbital insertion velocity at LEO boundary altitude. A planetary orbit at this ceiling takes roughly 2.4 hours. The line between 'flight' and 'orbit' has been crossed.

18,525 km/h — Mach 15.1, 800 km altitude. The Webwork provides flight energy through the Primordial Thread network — every cell contributes to propulsion. Near-orbital speed at medium Earth orbit altitude. The planet is below; the flight is orbital in character.

19,500 km/h — Mach 15.9, 1,500 km altitude. The Thread network means flight is a whole-body phenomenon — direction and speed are expressed through the entire physical form simultaneously, not through a single propulsion point.
20,500 km/h — Mach 16.7, 3,000 km altitude. At SS mid, orbital velocity is standard flight speed. Flight at this altitude exits the radiation belt interior. The planet is a curved surface below.

22,000 km/h — Mach 17.9, 5,000 km altitude. Medium-high Earth orbit zone. Flight at this altitude and speed is operationally equivalent to being a satellite. The World Rejection response to full aura output is measured in atmospheric events on the surface below.

24,700 km/h — Mach 20.2, 10,000 km altitude. SS ceiling — near geostationary orbit altitude. Flight at this speed and altitude at the boundary of medium and high Earth orbit. The planet occupies a fraction of the visual field.

25,935 km/h — Mach 21.2, 20,000 km altitude. The Collapse — body inside the Core — means flight propulsion draws from the Core anchor in Soul Space. The physical form moves through space as an expression of the Core's positional intent. GPS satellite orbit altitude.

28,000 km/h — Mach 22.9, 30,000 km altitude. The Unmaking rebuilt the body from atoms up — the aerodynamic properties of the rebuilt form are the intended aerodynamic properties. Flight at this altitude is trans-orbital.

30,000 km/h — Mach 24.5, 36,000 km altitude. At SSS mid, the flight speed approaches geostationary orbit velocity. The orbital period at this altitude and speed is 24 hours — the planet rotates at the same rate below.

31,500 km/h — Mach 25.7, 40,000 km altitude. Beyond geostationary orbit altitude. The planet is a small object at this flight ceiling. Dimensional distortion from transit at this speed is an observable navigational variable.

33,000 km/h — Mach 26.9, 50,000 km altitude. SSS ceiling — the Earth is the size of a fist at this altitude from a subjective standpoint. Flight at this ceiling is effectively interplanetary in scale. Dimensional wake persists after transit at this velocity.

domain.desc: 500 m radius. The Domain at A-rank entry is a localized field of reality alteration. Within the 500 m boundary, the Corebearer defines the parameters their techniques operate under. Opponents entering the boundary register the shift as pressure — passive resistance builds as they move inward. The domain requires active maintenance and is not free to hold at full output.

1,250 m radius. At A mid-lower, the domain has grown large enough to cover a full urban district. Environmental variables inside the boundary are partially subject to the Corebearer's intent — gravity direction, atmospheric density, kinetic friction coefficients can be locally adjusted. Deliberate entry by opponents below A-rank requires overcoming the passive boundary pressure.

2,000 m radius. 2 km domain boundary. The passive resistance at the edge is now strong enough that D-rank and below Corebearers cannot cross it under standard conditions. Within the domain, the Corebearer's techniques operate with reduced cost — the domain provides the environmental context that makes certain expressions easier.

2,750 m radius. The domain at A mid-upper covers terrain equivalent to a small town. Physical laws within the boundary can be selectively overwritten rather than nudged — not just adjusted, but replaced with a defined local rule. The energetic cost to maintain this is significant but sustainable at full A-rank reserve.

3,500 m radius. A ceiling — 3.5 km domain. Physical laws within the boundary are subject to full selective override. The outer edge of the domain registers as a wall of compressive pressure to entities below A-rank. Entry into the domain by such entities without the Corebearer's permission is a contested physical act, not a choice.

10 km radius. S-rank entry domain — the boundary now covers a city. The World Rejection pressure at the outer edge is measurable by instruments even in dormant mode. Within the boundary, reality modifications are comprehensive: spatial geometry, energetic interaction rules, and temporal density can be altered.
